agent_output.affected_group: Cruise ship medical staff, crew, passengers, and engineering staff on passenger vessels (13+ people) sailing from foreign ports to U.S. ports under CDC Vessel Sanitation Program
agent_output.change_summary: CDC 30-day Paperwork Reduction Act notice: submission to OMB of a proposed revision of the existing Maritime Illness Database and Reporting System (MIDRS) information collection (OMB 0920-1260, expiring 04/30/2022), refining respondent types, forms, recordkeeping and burden estimates; requests public comment within 30 days. No new substantive requirement is announced.

evidence.quote:
In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, the Centers 
for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has submitted the information 
collection request titled ``Maritime Illness Database and Reporting 
System (MIDRS)'' to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for 
review and approval.

This notice serves to allow an additional 30 days for public and 
affected agency comments.

This information collection request 
(ICR) is revised to refine and update respondent types, frequencies of 
responses, information collection forms, recordkeeping requirements, 
and time burden requested for AGE surveillance. CDC is also updating 
this ICR to include recordkeeping requirements related to VSP 
sanitation inspections.

this recordkeeping burden was not 
accurately accounted for in the prior ICR. There are no other costs to 
the respondents other than their time.

There are three types of respondents involved in AGE surveillance: 
Cruise ship medical staff or other designated personnel who treat and 
report AGE cases to VSP, and the cruise ship crew and the cruise ship 
passengers who may become AGE cases.

A fourth type of respondent is the cruise ship engineering staff 
who perform shipboard engineering and sanitation system maintenance.

Comments and recommendations for the proposed 
information collection should be sent within 30 days of publication of 
this notice to www.reginfo.gov/public/do/PRAMain.

uncertainties: Not classified as an event: routine PRA 30-day comment notice for revision of an existing information collection; no new legal requirement, deadline, or behavior change.

Large stated burden increase (5,591,150 hours) described as a more accurate estimate of existing practices; whether added recordkeeping requirements are new in substance cannot be determined from this document alone.
No effective date; OMB approval outcome not stated.
